correctness.rationale: For S=sum_{i=1}^n B_i+a B_{n+1}, a real, n>=1, we checked the partition: a=0 (n+1 points, modal mass c_n); a noninteger or |a|>n (2(n+1) disjoint points, modal mass c_n/2); integer |a|=k in [1,n] gives contiguous support n+k+1 and masses [binom(n,j)+binom(n,j-k)]/2^(n+1). The binomial estimates (n+1)c_n²<=3/4 and (n+floor(n/2)+1)c_n²<=1 follow via exact consecutive ratios; strictness for n=2,k=1 is direct. For k>floor(n/2) and n>=20, the proved Gaussian ratio bound p_n(j)<=c_n exp(-d(j)^2/n) implies M<3c_n/4, so K M²<27/32. Independently recomputed all 190 integer pairs with 1<=n<=19, inspecting exactly 3990 atom positions, exact worst ratio 3/4 at (n,k)=(1,1); this finite bridge exhausts the only unproved region, not the infinite n argument. Central binomial asymptotics with a=0 give H0/Hinf->2. Symmetry a versus -a and all real collision cases checked.
